text:
Partly. Satellite data show tree-cover loss of about 0.6 ha (3.4% of the 17.6 ha property) in 2022. It was corroborated: later years were observed, and the JRC 2020 forest map agrees across the whole loss area. The 2021 MGAP map classes about 0.5 ha of it as native forest and 0.1 ha as outside mapped forest. No planted forest was involved. A further 0.2 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha was detected but not counted as an event.

However, this does not establish that deforestation or land-use change occurred. Hansen loss includes any stand replacement, such as harvest or fire. The evidence also doesn't show the cause, legality, who was responsible, or any compliance status (e.g., EUDR). So: native-forest tree-cover loss is supported, but "deforestation" is not confirmed.
